- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- If forecast shows sharp spike followed by rapid decline, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to account for overshoot.
- If forecast mean is consistently below true mean over 3–5 days, apply upward bias of 2–5% to reflect mean reversion toward recent highs.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3–0.6), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, assume sentiment is bullish and increase next forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment momentum.
